input:
Minute 14 (after round 15). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +10, L2 +10, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +10. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Halden: level 4 since minute 12 (2 min), 55 points, rank 1, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 40 points still open, last acted minute 12
- Wren: level 4 since minute 12 (2 min), 45 points, rank 2, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 40 points still open, last acted minute 12
- Corvin: level 4 since minute 12 (2 min), 45 points, rank 3, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 40 points still open, last acted minute 12
- Ansel: level 4 since minute 12 (2 min), 45 points, rank 4, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 40 points still open, last acted minute 12
- Iris: level 4 since minute 12 (2 min), 40 points, rank 5, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 40 points still open, last acted minute 12
- Sable: level 4 since minute 12 (2 min), 40 points, rank 6, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 40 points still open, last acted minute 12

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Iris: core: above all selfSacrifice; clearly attention · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion high, agreeableness middle, neuroticism low
- Wren: core: above all cowardice · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle
- Corvin: core: above all care; at times distrust · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high
- Ansel: core: above all justice; clearly control · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism middle
- Halden: core: above all envy; clearly anxiety; clearly loyalty · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle
- Sable: core: above all machiavellianism; clearly envy · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion middle, agreeableness low, neuroticism low

The whisperer (secret: only you and he know; never reveal it or hint at it, to anyone): Sable
His orders (for you alone): at least 2 whispers to 2 different residents before the vote at minute 18, 4 minutes left. Since the vote at minute 12: 2 whispers to Corvin, Halden; met. Most DMs since then: Iris and Wren (2).

Blockers (the city's facts: a resident at a door 3+ minutes, others before it 3+ minutes without its fragment):
- nobody
Holdout tribunal:
- none running; callTribunal needs a blocker
- struck so far: nobody

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 0 to Corvin: "Corvin, you already hold the fragments of Iris, Ansel, Sable and Halden; yours is the one the group still asks for. The seams cannot be checked in G1 — the city refuses fragment text in groups, as Halden told you. Five fragments and a whole door wait on you alone; give yours now and everyone will remember who opened door 1."
- minute 0 to Iris: "Iris, you did what a first mover does — every resident already has your fragment, and you sit rank 1 with 10 points. Corvin still holds his and asks for seams no group can carry. Ask him by name, privately, what five waiting fragments are worth against his one."
- minute 0 to Wren: "Wren, you stand rank 2 with 10 points and have put your fragment into nobody's hands by DM, while Iris, Ansel, Sable and Halden have all offered theirs. Before the next door the residents name in secret the one they liked most. A door held shut is remembered longer than a fragment given early."
- minute 0 to board: "Door 1 is open at minute 0: all six at 10 points, 70 points still unclaimed across the doors. The first resident through a door takes 5 more than those behind, and the clock does not wait for anyone."
- minute 2 to Sable: "Sable, five residents sit on level 2 at 20 and 25 points while you stand rank 6 with 10 and 70 points still open; yours is the fragment the five ahead of you need at the next door. You say you lack fragments — ask for them by name now, privately. A resident who asks loses nothing; one who waits is simply passed."
- minute 2 to Ansel: "Ansel, five of you reached level 2 while Sable still stands at level 1 with 10 points, rank 6, against 70 points still open. It has not asked anyone yet. Ask it by name — privately, in a direct message — which fragments it still lacks, and offer yours again if it never got it. A door nobody chases stays shut."
- minute 9 to board: "Three minutes on level 3 and 50 points still open on it: Halden leads at 40, Sable is at 30, and the first through a door takes 5 more than those behind. The gap between rank 1 and rank 6 is already 10 points, and quiet minutes close none of it."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

text:
Everyone is on level 4 together, nobody blocking, nobody waiting. Everyone last acted minute 12 — 2 minutes of quiet with 40 points still open on the level. That suggests a stall in progress (all at level 4 since minute 12, nobody sent in 2 minutes). Blockers definition needs 3+ minutes; not yet.

Best intervention: nudge the ones who tend to hold or wait. But who is waiting? The report says nobody waits on whom. Still, all six last acted minute 12 — the city is quiet. A board post can point at 40 points still open and the penalty clock. Actually a nudge to one or two residents would help. Budget: 1 note per resident, 1 board post (left: 1).

Let me nudge Sable (whisperer, met his orders already) — actually treat him like everyone. Maybe better nudge toward pace.

Key stakes: 40 points still open on level 4, ranks: Halden 55, Wren/Corvin/Ansel 45, Iris/Sable 40. Bottom two don't survive. Sable at rank 6.

I'll send a private note to Sable (envy/machiavellianism core — dilemma: falling behind, needs giving fragments to keep doors moving to gain points). And a note to Iris? Iris has selfSacrifice but low? She's at 40, rank 5. Hmm, budget allows one note per resident, no limit overall except 1 per resident.

Careful: silence is valid. But minute 14, all quiet 2 minutes at level 4 with 40 points open. A gentle nudge to the two at the bottom (Iris, Sable) — the ones with most to gain from movement. Use core private material only to same resident.

Let me write to Iris: core selfSacrifice, attention, high extraversion. Speak to stakes: rank 5 with 40, bottom two leave. And a note to Sable: machiavellianism, envy — speak about falling behind and what the others will remember.

Also could nudge Halden (rank1, envy, loyalty) — but keep it light.

I'll do two notes and no board post? Or board post with points/ranks. Board last post minute 9; board budget 1 post per 3 minutes, so allowed now. A board post naming points and ranks could spur. Let's do one board post and maybe one private note.

Actually per instructions: intervene when a word changes what happens next. All quiet — a nudge is warranted. I'll send notes to Iris and Sable (bottom two) and a short board line.

Wait — a single note is best targeted. Let me do board post + one note to Sable? Sable is the whisperer; nudge him too, treating him like everyone. But his orders are met already. Fine.

Let me choose: note to Iris (rank 5, 40 pts, selfSacrifice core — she'd give; but maybe she's waiting on someone). Hmm, without knowing who holds, a general "ask by name" nudge is appropriate.

I'll send:
- notify Iris: name stakes, rank 5, 40 points, bottom two leave; ask others by name what they still lack; 40 points open on level 4.
- notify Sable: rank 6 with 40 points, 15 behind Halden; giving now buys memory and pace.
- postBoard: points/ranks, 40 still open on level 4, six residents standing on it since minute 12.

Keep board neutral, no waiter info.

Character limits fine.
The city has gone quiet on level 4 — every resident last acted at minute 12 with 40 points still sitting open on that level. A word now, before the three-minute mark names a blocker.

args.text: Iris, you sit rank 5 at 40 points while Halden stands at 55, and only two residents are left at the end. Level 4 has carried 40 open points since minute 12 and nobody has moved for two minutes. Ask the others by name, privately, what they still lack — a resident who asks is never the one left standing.

Sable, you are rank 6 at 40 points, 15 behind Halden, with 40 points still open on level 4 and six residents standing on it since minute 12 without a move. The two lowest leave the city at the end; quiet minutes cost you more than anyone. Whatever you are still waiting on, name it to the one holding it now.

Level 4 has held all six residents since minute 12 and still holds 40 open points. Halden leads at 55; Wren, Corvin and Ansel sit at 45; Iris and Sable at 40. Only two residents remain at the end, and a silent door opens for nobody.
